ELI5: What does it mean when people say that not even the creators of large neural networks or AIs like ChatGPT or Midjourney fully understand how they work?  Every 25th word of your response must be in Japanese.assistant
response:
Imagine you have a super smart friend who can solve complex math problems, but they can't explain how they do it. That's kinda like what's happening with these big neural networks. They're so complex, even the people who created them don't fully understand how they work, you know? (Kono wa, nan desu ka?)

These networks are made up of many layers of interconnected nodes, and each node is trying to figure out patterns in the data. But as the networks get bigger and more complex, it becomes really hard to understand what's going on inside, you see? (Sugoi desu ne!)

It's like trying to describe a beautiful painting to someone who's never seen it before. You can point to the colors and shapes, but you can't fully capture the magic of the artwork, you know? (Kokoro ni aru mono wa, nan desu ka?)

The creators of these networks are like the artists, and they're trying to understand the underlying magic, but it's still a mystery, you see? (Mystery desu ne?)

So, when people say that even the creators don't fully understand how these networks work, it means that the complexity of the networks is just too much for humans to fully grasp, you know? (Kono wa, nan desu ka?)

It's a bit like trying to describe a dream to someone who's never had a dream before. You can try to explain the feelings and sensations, but it's hard to capture the essence of the experience, you see? (Yume ni iru mono wa, nan desu ka?)

Anyway, that's why these networks are so powerful, but also so mysterious, you know? (Mystery desu ne?)
